scope: source-grounded authoring cards; not runtime verification

rooms.question: Can the same instructions draw a different plant?
rooms.ontology: An L-system rewrites symbols; a turtle interpreter assigns movements and turns to the resulting string.
rooms.action: Keep PRESET and GEN fixed while moving ANGLE; then hold ANGLE fixed and increase GEN once.
rooms.observable: Angle changes branch directions; generation count changes the rewritten string and its number of segments. The drawing is fitted back into its display.
rooms.mechanism: _generate applies every symbol replacement to a new string each generation; _draw_lsystem reads F/G as draw,+/- as turns,brackets as saved/restored state.
rooms.limit: A smaller drawn tree need not contain fewer instructions because the display normalises its bounds. The editor exposes presets, not arbitrary visitor rule-text editing.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Let the visitor compare the unchanged string under two interpreters, then author one replacement rule.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: How can descendants inherit a direction while becoming shorter?
rooms.ontology: A branching interpreter can carry numerical state such as step length, orientation and depth alongside its position.
rooms.action: Trace a branch from its base to its tips; compare an early fork with a deeper one.
rooms.observable: Branch lengths decrease with nesting depth and turns vary within a controlled range.
rooms.mechanism: _generate rewrites a preset string, resets random seed42; _draw_tree pushes full turtle state, multiplies length by length_decay on branch entry and restores it on exit.
rooms.limit: This displayed tree is generated from numerical rules, not grown by consuming resources or seeking light. A parametric interpreter is not by itself context-sensitive rewriting.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Show two trees with identical grammar and random seed but different length_decay, retaining their unnormalised lengths.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. No visitor sliders; use observation. Intended contextual-growth comparison can be developed with placed ContextSensitiveTree later.

rooms.question: Does an instruction contain its own meaning?
rooms.ontology: The same symbolic sentence can be interpreted with different movement conventions.
rooms.action: Compare the three labelled turtle drawings:25 degrees,45 degrees,and F means sidle. Find a branch correspondence across them.
rooms.observable: The same expanded sentence yields different directions and shapes; the sideways reader reinterprets forward movement.
rooms.mechanism: _ready rewrites one final string; _build_three_turtles calls _walk with changed angle and sideways flag; brackets restore position and heading.
rooms.limit: Similar labels do not make a perfectly controlled size comparison: step lengths differ and rendering stops after260 segments. The exhibit changes how a word is acted upon, not the string itself.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Invite the visitor to give F a fourth meaning, such as leaving a sound at a position, and compare what remains recognisable.

sources.fact: 33–43 shared string;117–163 three interpretations and260-segment cap.

rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. Static constructed comparison, no operable turtle controls promised.

rooms.question: What changes when a grammar makes corridors instead of branches?
rooms.ontology: A grammar can generate spatial relations without specifying a biological subject; an interpreter can map symbols to corridors and rooms.
rooms.action: Follow a corridor in the tabletop dungeon until it branches; compare a branch with a room and identify where a saved route resumes.
rooms.observable: A repeated grammar produces a network of small corridors, room slabs and walls.
rooms.mechanism: _generate_dungeon resolves grammar, produces string, interprets turtle segments and room positions, then normalises bounds to the display; default warren depth3.
rooms.limit: A diagram with corridor shapes has not been tested for inhabitation, accessibility or useful destinations. Counting rooms does not establish a good place to live.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Keep the grammar but reinterpret a dead end as a gathering place, then evaluate the resulting route from the visitor’s needs.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: Can identical kinds of growth meet different futures because they share a resource?
rooms.ontology: A growth rule is only part of a system; resource fields, timing and neighbours can constrain when it runs.
rooms.action: Watch neighbouring trees and the soil display over several growth steps; compare their branch development and recorded health.
rooms.observable: Trees grow in turn, draw on shared nutrients, and can stop at different stages.
rooms.mechanism: _grow_step consumes nutrients, changes diameter, expands grammar only if nutrients>0.05 and season is not winter, applies competition and records health; _process diffuses/replenishes nutrients and advances seasons.
rooms.limit: The model chooses what counts as a resource and competition. Its round-robin schedule is also a condition, and finite maximum generations must not be mistaken for ecological maturity.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare competition and shared-resource cooperation under the same initial field and measure a chosen collective outcome.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. No visitor ecosystem slider verified. Do not present simulated health as biological measurement.

rooms.question: When you change a tree, which choices are yours and which were built into the tool?
rooms.ontology: A parameterised phenotype is a form generated from a finite set of numerical traits; choosing traits differs from changing the rules that interpret them.
rooms.action: Move one branch-angle or branching-depth slider and watch the preview; change one trait at a time before trying RANDOM.
rooms.observable: Each slider edits a named gene-like parameter and rebuilds the preview after a short delay; RANDOM replaces the parameter set.
rooms.mechanism: _apply_slider_to_dna maps normalised controls into trait ranges; TreeMorphology.build interprets DNA. PLANT saves Engine metadata and flashes preview, rather than itself placing a new tree.
rooms.limit: The sliders bound what variation can become visible. Calling parameters genes does not make the tool a genetic evolutionary process; pressure defaults none.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Offer two different trait-to-form mappings for the same parameter values and let visitors choose a value the existing fitness functions do not reward.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. PLANT downstream catalyst pickup is unverified; avoid promising automatic planting.

rooms.question: How much of a pattern belongs to the rule, and how much to the marks it chooses?
rooms.ontology: An alphabet is the set of visible marks through which a selection rule is expressed.
rooms.action: Watch a new row of the textile appear, then trace a diagonal path made by neighbouring marks. Identify where your eye connects marks the program selected separately.
rooms.observable: Rows of two diagonal orientations accumulate into a maze-like cloth and scroll downward.
rooms.mechanism: Each cell compares a random draw with odds(default0.5), chooses a mark and colour; _process advances every0.18s and weaves a fresh row.
rooms.limit: The visual path is not a solved maze or an L-system rewriting history. Two chosen marks can generate relations that no individual choice explicitly planned.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Keep the same seeded choices but replace diagonals with orthogonals or blocks; ask what new uses and readings the same choices allow.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. One physical loom artifact carries the assemblage question; no mandatory explanation of every gallery object.
